evidence.claim: Most of the present NC 12 began as sand road, paved during the 1950s and early 1960s.
evidence.quote: Most of the current route of Highway 12 was originally a sand road until it was paved through the 1950s and early 1960s.

evidence.claim: The current route appeared on the 1964 map between Ocracoke and Whalebone and reached the mainland connection with U.S. 70 in 1976.
evidence.quote: The current NC 12 shows up on the 1964 map running from Ocracoke to Whalebone. In 1976 NC 12 was extended onto the mainland to connect with US 70

evidence.claim: Maintaining that connection has required changes: the Rodanthe Bridge opened in 2022, replacing a section repeatedly closed by overwash, flooding and sand.
evidence.quote: The bridge, known as the Rodanthe Bridge, opened on July 28, 2022, and spans 2.4 miles (3.9 km) of the Pamlico Sound.  It replaced a section of NC 12 known for frequent closures due to overwash, flooding, and sand accumulation.

evidence.claim: Traveling south from Whalebone Junction, NC 12 crosses Oregon Inlet, passes Pea Island and bypasses Rodanthe before reaching Avon and Buxton.
evidence.quote: It bypasses the community of Rodanthe using the Rodanthe Bridge. It crosses the New Inlet bridge onto Pea Island and 11 miles (18 km) further north is the Marc Basnight Bridge over Oregon Inlet, connecting Pea Island to Bodie Island.

evidence.claim: Traveling south from Whalebone Junction, NC 12 crosses Oregon Inlet, passes Pea Island and bypasses Rodanthe before reaching Avon and Buxton.

flags: Guidebook cache files 00–03 have identical bodies ending in the Flat Rock section; the Outer Banks pages implied by their URL fragments are absent. Dropped the Alexander Midgett whale-skeleton/Model T anecdote and the observation that old workboats fill Atlantic Harbor.

Dropped Hatteras ferry duration of about 40 minutes and Cedar Island duration of about 2.25 hours: absent from the available guidebook text; Ocracoke page instead says one hour for Hatteras. FHWA total travel estimate is attributed.

Cape Hatteras Lighthouse page mixes tower heights and measurement baselines (198, 200, 208, 210 feet) and has inconsistent first-light chronology. Height, superlative and first-light date omitted; completion in 1870 and move in 1999 retained.
Atlantic kept as a short, evidence-limited fishing-community moment. Its current fish-house status comes only from Wikipedia, not a fresh operator source.
Practical ferry note was checked against cached sources only on 2026-10-11; no live schedule or access verification was possible.

NC 12 and byway extents differ. Used byway endpoint at U.S. 70/Merrimon Road rather than implying the designation extends into Beaufort. FHWA and Wikipedia give different route lengths; distance omitted. Material Otway mileage is inconsistent with its geography; not used.
